_note: The in-target gate's mapping (workplan 0116 T4, the relay's first slice, proved on the real stack). A FOURTH mapping beside the archive-import and zip-route ones: the same five-file Takeout, as the same two-part .zip download, but this time the parts are NOT on the appliance's disk at all — the gate PUTs them into the e2e-target Nextcloud first, and `where: "target"` makes the path relative to this migration's own file target. So the pass reads them over the wire by byte range (PROPFIND, GET with Range), which is what a managed pass does after the relay lands the parts: no volume, no local path, nothing of the archive on our disk. Its target is a SUBFOLDER, from-target/, and the parts sit in from-target/exports/ — where the relay would leave them, and where the import must never touch them (hard rule 2). Loads PAUSED like every mapping; green-lit only by its own gate, which runs after the zip-route gate. e2e.yml writes it under a name that sorts after every other mapping; the gates select by id, never by position.
